absent: Full clone and unshare flag matrix, argument validation and system call entry behavior beyond the tail linkage and namespace checks shown.
Internals of scheduler, cgroup, security, audit, performance, tracing, probe, memory, IO and connector hooks invoked before and after linkage.
Complete layouts and lifetime rules for task, signal, sighand, pid, namespace and credential objects beyond fields touched here.
Locking, reference counting and reaping rules for namespaces, mounts, IPC, network, time and cgroup subsystems outside the shown sections.
PID filesystem integration, pidfd handling and process connector message formats beyond installation and notification calls.

findings.text: Provides namespace handling for task creation. When no new namespace class is requested and time scoping permits sharing it retains the current aggregate and reports success. Otherwise it enforces administrative privilege, rejects incompatible IPC isolation with shared semaphore undo, creates a fresh aggregate and installs it on the task with time handling for separate memory.

Reserves and publishes a hierarchical process identifier for a target namespace chain. It validates optional caller supplied values per level for range and privilege, reserves hidden slots, then publishes the complete object and holds an active reference on the namespace, reporting distinct failures for invalid request, denial, exhaustion, collision and interruption.
Determines whether a user namespace is nested within a claimed ancestor by ascending parent links from the child until ancestor depth is reached and testing identity equality.

Initializes kernel thread bookkeeping on a new task and reports whether setup succeeded. It rejects tasks that already carry such state, allocates a control record, prepares exit and park completions plus an affinity queue element, and links task and control in both directions with allocation origin recorded.

Creates the per processor idle task during early boot with shared memory and marks for kernel idle execution using a start routine that never runs. On success it binds every identifier class of the new task to the global initial identifier and completes idle state setup for the given processor.

Spawns an IO worker that shares filesystem, file table, signal handling, memory and IO context with its creator, stays grouped with the creator threads and remains untraced. The new execution context is flagged for IO work and user worker scheduling.

Describes bidirectional linkage between a task and its kernel thread control. The task side holds a private control pointer and an exit completion pointer, while the control side holds the owning task pointer, the allocation node, completions for exit and park events and a list element for affinity management.

Defines the per task namespace aggregate as references for mount, host identity, IPC, child PID, cgroup, network and child time plus current time. A fresh aggregate starts with a single reference count and each member is either shared with an added reference or replaced by a newly created namespace with ordered release on failure.

Defines a logical identifier as an array of numeric values with one entry per namespace level from root to target, each entry pairing a number with its namespace. The object also carries a reference count, a protective lock, per type task link sets, a wait queue for descriptor waits and auxiliary filesystem linkage.

Final task linkage requires exclusive task list protection with interrupts masked, with the creator signal handler lock nested inside. Timestamps are captured before exclusivity begins, and both protections are released only after parent links, identifier attachments and global fork and thread counters are stable.
Reset of per task latency tracing is serialized by a dedicated latency lock taken with interrupt state saved, covering both clearing of the record storage and resetting of the record count.

Identifier table mutation is serialized by a global map lock with allocation memory preloaded, allowing one retry with reclaimable memory on exhaustion. Attachment of a task to its identifier object requires exclusive task list hold, which the implementation asserts.

Duplication of host identity holds a dedicated semaphore for reading while the name is copied. Creation of per level identifier caches uses a dedicated mutex around the check and create sequence with a shared pointer rechecked after locking.

Unprivileged sharing is permitted only when no new namespace class except possibly user isolation is requested and either memory is shared or child time already matches current time. Other new namespace requests need administrative capability in the task user namespace, and combined new IPC isolation with shared semaphore undo is invalid.

A new PID namespace derives its level from its parent, must remain within ancestry of the creator user namespace and within the maximum depth, and must obtain a counted allocation. It starts in an adding state with an empty table, a default maximum, an active reference on parent and user namespaces, and a deferred destruction work item.

PID namespace inheritance shares the previous namespace when no new PID isolation is requested. A request for new isolation is accepted only when the creator active namespace equals the previous namespace, otherwise it fails as invalid.

Host identity is shared with an added reference when no new isolation is requested. When new isolation is requested a fresh namespace is cloned from the old name and the old reference is released, with distinct failures for quota exhaustion, allocation failure and common initialization error.

A group leader is added to the parent child list and the global task list with group, process group and session attachments and the process count advanced. A non leader is added to the shared signal thread set with thread and liveness counts advanced and is made to participate in any ongoing group stop.

Parent assignment and exit notification follow creation mode. When reuse of the creator parent is requested the real parent and execution lineage come from the creator, with thread creation suppressing notification and non thread reuse inheriting the group leader value. Otherwise the creator becomes the real parent and the caller supplied notification value applies.

A new leader inherits delayed shared signals, terminal reference, subreaper ancestry from its real parent and optional automatic reaping. A namespace initial process is installed as namespace reaper under exclusive access and marked unkillable.
Confinement state is duplicated after fallibility ends under signal protection, and future privilege gain is suppressed when requested by creation mode.

After global locks are released, association with the cgroup hierarchy is required to precede scheduler introduction so scheduler extensions observe membership. Descriptor installation, connector and performance notifications, tracing hooks and memory pressure adjustment accompany this handoff.

Overlimit testing clamps the supplied ceiling to the signed maximum and ascends the user namespace ownership chain. It reports overlimit when any level shows a negative mark or exceeds the current ceiling, otherwise it narrows the ceiling to that level maximum before continuing.

A new thread observes group stop state of its shared signal owner. An active stop count is incremented and consume semantics are added to its pending mask, a stopped flag without active count still propagates pending stop, and a running state leaves the newcomer without added stop state.
Latency reset clears the per task record storage and its count under lock. Accounting reset clears elapsed and memory integral accumulators, with no locking shown in the examined fragment.

Each PID namespace publishes its identifier maximum through a private duplicated control table bound to its own storage with the set marked seen. Per depth identifier caches are named by level, sized for the level plus one entries, and created once with cache alignment and accounting behavior.

Creation moves from fallible preparation to an infallible linked phase once namespace liveness and fatal signal checks pass. Earlier failures unwind through scheduler release, cgroup cancellation, descriptor and identifier release, threading and memory teardown, signal and filesystem release and credential and accounting release before returning the stored error with task marked dead.

Identifier allocation moves from range and privilege validation to hidden reservation and then to publication. Slots are reserved with empty placeholders invisible to lookup, first process and liveness rules are enforced, and only then are slots switched to the real object with per namespace allocation counts advanced.

A namespace starts in adding state with cursor reset and allocation count at its marker. Each publication advances the count out of the marker, while reaping that clears the marker causes later reservation and linkage attempts to fail with resource exhaustion rather than waking a departed reaper.
Capturing start timestamps before the task becomes globally visible prevents user space from predicting start time by delaying creation between timestamp capture and linkage.

Reaping of the target namespace between identifier reservation and linkage could cause a missed termination, so linkage rechecks liveness. A pending fatal signal on the creator independently aborts creation with interruption status.

Publishing identifiers only after all levels are assigned prevents lookup from finding a partially initialized object. Empty placeholders reserve table positions and the switch to the complete object occurs under the table lock.

Fact: usable identifiers begin at one with a small low range reserved for early system tasks, allocation wraps past that floor once the cursor advances beyond it, value one must exist before any other value in a fresh namespace, and each namespace enforces its own configurable maximum.

Fact: creation of PID and UTS namespaces is charged to distinct per user namespace counters keyed by creator identity, and task creation is charged to the process number limit with the charge released on failure.
Fact: each PID namespace maintains a configurable identifier maximum initialized from the global ceiling bounded below by a per processor default scaled by possible processor count.
